When the Buddha was about to pass into Parinibbana, the twin Sal trees bloomed out of season and rained blossoms over his body to honor him. Heavenly beings gathered in the sky to shower divine flowers and play celestial music. Monks, nuns, and lay followers also came from all around to pay their final respects and bow before him.

Before passing away, the Buddha told his followers that everything in the world breaks down, so they must work hard with mindfulness. He also said his teachings and rules would be their teacher after he was gone.

Children can use mindfulness every day to stay safe and make good choices. It helps them focus on their schoolwork and listen carefully to parents and teachers. It also helps them control their anger so they can be kind to their friends.

The Buddha gave this advice because everything in life changes and ends and mindfulness keeps us from making bad choices and helps us do good. It was the best tool the Buddha could leave behind to keep his followers safe and peaceful.
The Buddha passed away into Parinibbana in the Sal Grove of the Malla kings in Kushinagar on the Tuesday of the Full Moon day of Kason.

When we walk, talk, or work, we focus only on the present moment. Before we act, we pause to make sure our words and choices are kind and useful. When bad thoughts like anger or sadness start, we notice them and gently let them go. By staying mindful, we stay calm, avoid mistakes, and bring peace to ourselves and others.
it means the final death of a Buddha or enlightened person after which they leave behind all suffering and are never reborn again.

Under the Bodhi Tree, the Buddha to be sat and meditated. Bad spirits tried to stop him, but he defeated them. On a full moon night, he learned the ultimate truth about life and erased all bad thoughts. That is how he became the holy Buddha.

The Buddha founded the Sangha to protect and share his teachings so they would last long after his passing. He organized it by creating clear discipline rules to keep the monks and nuns united, peaceful, and focused on spiritual practice.
